title: Eisenkot Cancels Planned Likud Coalition Meeting After Netanyahu’s Knesset Speech
dek: Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party called off a scheduled negotiating session with Likud, citing Netanyahu’s speech at the swearing-in of the 26th Knesset, as Eisenkot continues to pursue a coalition.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Portrait of Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot

keyPoints: Yashar, led by Gadi Eisenkot, announced Tuesday that a preliminary negotiating meeting with Likud had been scheduled, then canceled it after Netanyahu’s Knesset speech, the Jerusalem Post reported.
Eisenkot called the speech “delusional, divisive, hateful, and disgraceful”; Yashar said Netanyahu “does not want unity.”
Likud said Netanyahu would “turn over every stone” for national unity and called the cancellation “puzzling” given Yashar’s talks with Arab parties.
Eisenkot’s bloc has submitted requests to replace Knesset Speaker Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, with a vote expected within the coming week, the Times of Israel reported.
body:
Talks to form Israel’s next government took a sharp turn on Tuesday after Yashar, the party led by Gadi Eisenkot, canceled a negotiating session with Likud.

## Meeting scrapped

Yashar announced Tuesday that it had scheduled a preliminary meeting with Likud, [the Jerusalem Post reported](https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/politics-and-diplomacy/article-914502). After Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech at the Knesset, the party said Eisenkot had instructed that the meeting planned for Wednesday be canceled. The party cited its own four principles for forming a government.

Netanyahu had called on opposition leaders on Monday to join a single unified government, saying it was needed “in the need of the hour.” In Tuesday’s speech he also argued for a unity government in the face of an Iranian nuclear threat, which he said must be destroyed.

## Both sides trade charges

Yashar said Netanyahu “will always choose himself” and accused him of dividing Israeli citizens. Likud responded that it was “willing to meet with representatives of any faction that desires unity,” and called it “puzzling” that the opposition was canceling a meeting with Likud while advancing negotiations with Arab parties. According to the same report, Arab parties walked out during the national anthem immediately after the swearing-in.

## Where the process stands

Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government on Sunday, giving him 28 days, which can be extended by 14. Eisenkot and his partners command a parliamentary majority, the [Times of Israel](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-10-2026/) reported, and have sought to replace Speaker Ohana with a vote expected within the coming week. Eisenkot has also named Matan Kahana for the speaker’s post, a choice the [Jerusalem Post](https://www.jpost.com/israel-election-2026/article-914614) said could complicate efforts to bring haredi parties into a coalition.

## What to watch

Two near-term markers will show whether the process moves forward. The first is the vote to replace Speaker Ohana, which Eisenkot’s bloc has requested and which the Times of Israel reported is expected within the coming week. The second is the 28-day window Herzog granted Eisenkot on Sunday, which can be extended by 14 days.

Whether Likud and Yashar return to the negotiating table after the canceled meeting remains unresolved. Netanyahu has said he is committed to a national unity government, and Yashar has said it will continue its own negotiations on the four principles it has set out.

## Security cabinet and a Thursday briefing (Nov. 12)

KAN reported Wednesday evening that Israel's security cabinet had instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, [Anadolu reported](https://aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-security-cabinet-orders-military-to-prepare-for-possible-attack-on-iran-report/4121434). The directive followed Eisenkot's letter to Netanyahu urging him to refrain from unnecessary military operations until a new government is formed. In the letter, Eisenkot wrote that Netanyahu "no longer enjoys the confidence of the Knesset," with only 46 lawmakers supporting him as prime minister. Netanyahu's office called the letter "an irresponsible move."

KAN said the security cabinet is expected to convene Sunday for the first time since Oct. 5, [Anadolu reported](https://aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-cabinet-to-meet-sunday-amid-opposition-fears-of-strike-on-iran/4121972). Opposition figures have accused Netanyahu of possibly seeking military action to strengthen his position; Netanyahu's office has rejected that characterization.

On Thursday, Eisenkot and Netanyahu met for about two hours at Netanyahu's office in Jerusalem, Anadolu reported, citing a statement from Netanyahu's office and Eisenkot. The statement said Eisenkot "was briefed on the security and diplomatic challenges facing the State of Israel at this time," and that the two sides would continue to exchange updates as needed. The meeting followed Eisenkot's request for intervention by Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to secure regular security briefings. Whether Likud and Yashar return to formal coalition talks remains unresolved.
